title: "How CI works"
description: "Public validation, review and delivery evidence for contributors."

GitHub Actions selects relevant checks from the repository workflows. Detailed operator runbooks are maintained privately.

## Validation and Delivery Evidence

Validate the exact source being proposed with the relevant focused checks. Record the commands and their outcomes, and distinguish local checks, CI, deployment identity and production behavior. A successful source check alone is not evidence of a deployment. Keep independent review and applicable release gates.

## Label-gated heavy PR CI (`ready-for-ci`)

Heavy PR workflows require the `ready-for-ci` label. Non-draft pull requests from the same repository are eligible on `opened` and `ready_for_review`; forks are excluded from automatic admission. Independent review and green exact-head CI remain separate merge requirements. Run focused pre-push checks on an admitted development machine to reduce avoidable first-run failures. Skipped checks are not executed verification.

`auto-ready-for-ci.yaml` labels eligible pull requests using live pull-request metadata. It runs hosted metadata-only code from the base branch, without checking out or executing PR code. It is always-on admission automation rather than an affected-path validation job. Configure `CI_ADMISSION_TOKEN` as a token scoped only to this repository, with issues write and pull requests read permissions. A GitHub App installation token requires an existing rotation supplier; a fine-grained token requires expiry and renewal ownership. No token is created or installed by the workflow. Do not reuse the release administrator token.

The separate token is required because labels written with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger the `labeled` CI event. A missing admission token fails visibly; there is no fallback that adds a label without starting CI. Already-labelled PRs are unchanged. Before activation, the token supplier and independent workflow review must be accepted. An operator may add the label through the existing authenticated GitHub route while that supplier is unavailable.

Public pull-request jobs use GitHub-hosted runners. Self-hosted CI is restricted to trusted `push` or `workflow_dispatch` jobs on `main`; it must not execute fork PR code or receive production secrets. Machine admission and production-host headroom remain mandatory.

## Authorized CI Queue Cleanup

Cancellation needs explicit authorization for its scope. Identify each run and its source before acting, preserve required release and deployment work, and record the observed outcome. A branch name alone does not establish that a run is redundant.

## Draft PR runner admission

Draft status defers heavy verification where configured. Security eligibility and required checks follow the checked-in workflows. Moving a PR out of draft does not itself establish review approval or successful verification.

## Hosted runner reservation and PR queue pressure

Batch reviewable changes and use authorized local or development-runner checks to reduce PR queue pressure. Queue position and concurrency settings do not guarantee release capacity. Preserve the source identity and evidence for every reported result.

## Meet, Lettin, and Parley Cloudflare validation

App validation covers the affected application and its dependencies. Verify build metadata against the candidate source where required. Local tests, emitted artifacts and deployed behavior are distinct evidence; passing one does not establish the others.

## PR runner pool: variable, canary and kill switch

PR verification can use a separately admitted runner pool. Routing follows trusted workflow policy and must preserve isolation for untrusted contributions. Pool routing does not replace the PR label gate or independent review. Operator configuration and recovery procedures are maintained privately.

## Report-only Web E2E

The report-only Web browser workflow runs smoke or broader browser verification according to its trigger. It supplies browser evidence; it does not deploy the application. Its workflow-specific runtime exception does not resume other paused runtimes.

## Repository cache budget

CI caches reduce repeated downloads and setup work. Cache availability is not guaranteed, and eviction can require fresh downloads. Reusing a cache never substitutes for checking the candidate source and dependency identity.

## Frozen workflow installs

Workflow dependency installs use `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, and the retry helper adds the flag to project installs. Deliberate lockfile regeneration and pinned global CLI installs must match an exact workflow file, step name and full command in `scripts/ci/frozen-bun-install-exceptions.json`, and every exception disables lifecycle scripts. Run `node --test scripts/ci/frozen-bun-install-guard.test.js` to check the policy. Release credentials are scoped to the steps that push; operator details are maintained privately.

## CI summary

The `CI summary` check is one check run on the pull request head. `.github/workflows/ci-summary-poster.yml` computes it from the default branch. The workflow token is `contents: read`. It is not a `workflow_run` consumer. A dedicated GitHub App installation token posts the check. The job checks out the default branch only and does not run pull request code.

The check stays in progress while the pull request is a draft, an expected workflow has not started, or a run or check is still open. A completed workflow fails the summary when its conclusion is not success, including skipped and neutral. A completed check fails the summary unless its conclusion is success, skipped, or neutral. The summary succeeds only when every expected run is success and no other completed run or check on that head is failing. Expected workflows are the active default-branch workflows whose `pull_request` trigger matches the base branch, labels, and changed paths. An unreadable trigger stays expected. The summary's own check and workflow run are ignored. Path matching can over-match, which waits for more workflows instead of going green early.

`pull_request_target` posts the current picture. A schedule at minutes 7, 22, 37, and 52 refreshes every open pull request. GitHub may delay or drop a scheduled run, so a settled result can lag.

Until these repository secrets exist, the poster job skips and logs "App not configured". It posts nothing and does not borrow another app's credentials. A partial or malformed configuration still fails closed:

- `CI_SUMMARY_APP_ID`: the GitHub App's numeric id.
- `CI_SUMMARY_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`: that app's PEM private key.

Create the app for this repository, not as a grant of `checks: write` on the shared Actions token. Install it on `tutur3u/platform` with Actions read, Checks read and write, Contents read, Metadata read, and Pull requests read. Store the two secrets as Actions secrets. The deleted workflow id `407998590` stays deleted; this poster is a different file.

### Test and Type Check draft admission

Test and Type Check defer every validation job while a pull request is a draft,
even if `ready-for-ci` remains present. `ready_for_review` admits validation once
the readiness label is present; `converted_to_draft` cancels superseded PR work
and starts a skipped run. Protected branch pushes retain validation. Check names
and aggregate failure assertions remain stable. Regression coverage:
`scripts/ci/test-type-draft-admission.test.js`.

The trusted App admission path must keep `opened` and `ready_for_review`: its App
label write generates the real `pull_request:labeled` event. Security classification
continues on drafts and bot-authored PRs. Summary metadata events retain draft and
label transitions so the displayed readiness state stays accurate.

### Opt-in Test and Type Check runners

`CI_VALIDATION_RUNNER` selects only the secret-free PR unit shards and PR Type
Check job. Empty, malformed or unsupported values retain `ubuntu-latest`; pushes
and forks remain hosted. Allowed `ttr-selfhosted-<host>` values are defined by `HOST_LABELS` in
`scripts/ci/self-hosted-policy.js`. Leave the variable unset until a runner is
registered and independently qualified. Clearing it restores hosted selection for new jobs.
This source change does not register runners or change fork approval settings.

The routing condition requires a PR with matching head/base repository IDs and
names. Jobs explicitly grant only `contents: read`, carry no secrets or tokened
Turbo inputs, disable persistent Bun caching and retain restore-only PR Turbo
caches. Push jobs carrying credentials remain hosted. The required Test root-script job runs
`scripts/ci/self-hosted-policy.js` across all workflows; regression tests include
missing guards, elevated permissions, secret references, cache writers, fork
fallback and invalid variable controls. Source tests establish policy behavior;
actual host qualification and execution require separate runtime evidence.

## Calendar owning-suite timings

The `calendar-native` job in `mail-calendar-tasks-builds.yaml` reports Calendar,
Web and shared Tasks UI tests as three sequential steps after supplier builds,
the native Calendar build and the tracked route-tree drift guard. Each suite
inherits the job's production profile and CI fixtures. Default success conditions
keep emitted-config qualification, binding and consumer type checks, artifact
sealing, runtime acceptance and restore qualification behind successful tests.

Step separation has zero expected green-path saving. Measure each suite on the
same exact-commit CI run before proposing parallelism, including supplier/build
and artifact-transfer costs. Preserve the generated route tree used by the accepted
build in any future handoff. OAuth tests skipped without integration credentials
provide no integration coverage. Regression coverage is in
`scripts/ci/calendar-suite-steps.test.mjs`, loaded by the artifact regressions.
